Nigerian beauty queen, Damilola Bolarinde, has been named Miss International Africa 2026 after representing the country at the 64th edition of the Miss International pageant in Tokyo, Japan. The Miss International organisation announced her continental title on Thursday, following the grand finale held on November 25, where 73 contestants competed for the international crown. Bolarinde, who finished among the Top 20 finalists, was named Miss International Africa despite not advancing to the Top 10. Reacting to her pageant experience, the model shared an emotional message on her Instagram page on Wednesday, expressing excitement about reaching the grand finale. She wrote, “Some moments are too powerful to be just dreams, this is destiny calling! Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. This is the time! It is the grand finale!” I have what it takes to win Miss Universe 2026 – Danielle Adewusi S’African protesters demand Adetshina’s exit VIDEO: I have been treated unfairly, targeted in South Africa, says Chidimma Adetshina Bolarinde, also known as Queen Dammy, represented Lagos State at the 2025 Miss Universe Nigeria pageant, where she emerged first runner-up behind Onyinyechi Basil, who represented Anambra State and won the competition. She also won Miss Grand Nigeria 2022 and represented Nigeria at the Miss Grand International pageant in Vietnam, where she made the Top 20. In April 2026, she won the Face of Hope pageant, securing the Miss International Nigeria 2026 title and the opportunity to represent the country at the international competition. The grand finale, held on April 19 at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos, saw Bolarinde emerge ahead of Miss Anambra, who finished as first runner-up, and Miss Rivers, who came third. A professional model, actress and entrepreneur, Bolarinde is also the founder of The Unconventional Quest, an advocacy initiative that encourages young people to explore non-traditional career paths. Meanwhile, Elizaveta Kuznetsova of Moldova won the Miss International 2026 crown, making history as the first representative of her country to claim the title. Brittany Feeney of the United Kingdom emerged first runner-up, followed by Laura Glozarová of the Czech Republic as second runner-up, Victoria Kosasieputri of Indonesia as third runner-up and Khánh Như Lê of Vietnam as fourth runner-up.
